title.narrative: The Young Women for Awareness, Agency, Advocacy, and Accountability (YW4A) Programme

description.narrative: Influence the adoption, amendment, withdrawal or effective utilisation and implementation of laws and policies towards promoting young women’s rights to leadership, participation and ending SGBV in Kenya by 2025.

The programme aims to strengthen and diversify young women’s participation and amplify their voices to effectively influence decision-making towards gender-just laws, policies, norms, and practices related to their bodily integrity and equal participation.

title.narrative: WRGE 1.1. (WRG001) #of laws blocked, adopted or improved to eradicate all forms of violence against women and girls in public and private life;

description.narrative: Advocacy towards reform under the Sexual Offences Act on the age of consent, introduce a “Romeo and Juliet” clause and to repeal Section 43(5) to recognize marital rape.Better implementation of legislation on GBV including the Sexual Offences Act, Witness Protection Act, Victim Protection Act and Protection Against Domestic Violence Act.

comment.narrative: 1. Section 43(5) of the Sexual Offences Act precludes sexual violence within marriage, which contradicts the Constitution of Kenya and the Protection Against Domestic Violence Act which defines violence to include sexual violence within marriage. There is therefore a need to repeal this section to ensure that married women who experience violence access justice and perpetrators are held accountable.2. Recently, there have been debates in Kenya on the alleged disproportionate punishment of boys who have sexual relations with girls and court judgments including from the Court of Appeal on romeo and juliet clauses and the proposal to lower the age of consent. We will take part in the amendments of the Sexual Offences Act to provide clarity on the age of consent and provide for romeo and juliet clauses that are in line with international human rights standards and the best interest of the child.
no changes
Review of the Sexual Offences Act underway through the National Councul on the Administration of Justice's Committee on the Review of Laws on Sexual Offences and Gender-Based Violence.

Advocacy towards the repealing of Section 43)5) of the Sexual Offences Act to criminalize marital rape.Engagement in the legal reform process of the Sexual Offences Act to provide clarity on the age of consent and romeo-and-juliet clause.

WROs and young women have been engaging in advocacy on marital rape, the age of consent and romeo-and juliet clauses in collaboration with the national Generation Equality Forum CSO working group and with the NCAJ committee on the review of the Sexual Offences Act and GBV legislation.

title.narrative: WRGE 1.1 (WRG001) # of by-laws to eradicate all forms of violence against women and girls in public and private life are better implemented as a result of CSO engagement.

description.narrative: WRGE 1.1 (WRG001) # of by-laws to eradicate all forms of violence against women and girls in public and private life are better implemented as a result of CSO engagement. Better implementation of the Migori and Meru County Policies on Sexual and Gender Based Violence.

comment.narrative: County governments in Kenya have a role to play in addressing SGBV as captured under the National Gender and Equality Commission’s Model Policy on SGBV for County Governments. Meru and Migori Counties were the first and third Counties in Kenya to adopt SGBV Policies, demonstrating political ownership and goodwill in addressing SGBV. The policies set up coordination structures and an implementation framework to prevent and respond to SGBV. However, the Policies are not effectively and adequately implemented and many of their provisions remain paper rights and are not translated into lived realities. The programme will therefore advocate for the better implementation of these frameworks to ensure that SGBV is prevented, properly addressed in a survivor-centrerd way an that there is enhanced access to services and justice.
no changes

Meru County designated an SGBV Court as part of the implementation of the SGBV Policy.Migori County Government currently reviewing the SGBV Policy to identify areas for reform and better implementation.
Revisions to the Sexual Offences Act: Repeal of Section 43(5) (to criminalise marital rape, block the lowering of the age of consent and improve “Romeo-and-Juliet” (close in age) clauses

Some positive progress was made on revisions of the law during 2024. As of July 2025, the review committee was still working on the final draft of the amendment bill. That committee is headed by the National Council for Administration of Justice (NCAJ) but it is multisectoral with some CSOs including Equality Now and is chaired by a member of women’s rights NGO FIDA-Kenya who is committed to include reforms on marital rape, femicide and other issues. The prospects for the inclusions in the bill of the clauses we are promoting on age of consent and “Romeo and Juliet” exemptions seem good, with the definition of close in age exception having been included in the draft amendment bill, but the criminalisation of marital rape may not proceed. Preliminary discussions pointed to the committee not wanting to remove the current exemption, Section 43 (5), due to the fear that MPs will reject the whole bill if they do so.
Migori County Policy on Sexual and Gender Based ViolenceMeru County Policy on Sexual and Gender Based Violence

WROs and young women in Meru and Migori counties have underaken advocacy with county and national government actors including multi-sectoral structures such as the County Gender Sector Working Group ands and Court Users Committee. The advocacy was done ith a view to highlighting the root causes and drivers of SGBV and the challenges experienced in the prevention, referral pathway and access to justice chain. These advocacy actions have resulted in various initiatives aimed at the better implementation of the two policies including the establishment of a Specialized SGBV Court in Meru, the beginning of the development of SGBV Bills to support the Policies and attendant resources required for their operationalization.

title.narrative: WRGE 1.1. (WRG003): # of by-laws blocked, adopted, improved to eradicate all forms of violence against women and girls in public and private life

description.narrative: Development and adoption of Kisii County Policy on Sexual and Gender-Based Violence.Better implementation of the Migori and Meru County Policies on Sexual and Gender Based Violence.

comment.narrative: NB: In the baseline report, these key laws on sexual and gender based violence were noted to require better implementation as many provisions, especially of the WPA, VPA and PaDVA have not been operationlized. However they are not advocacy priorities under the programme.
Adoption of the a Kisii County Gender Policy

A good draft policy was developed in 2023 and disseminated to government departments and the public. A key event in the drafting process was a drafting workshop through a retreat convened by YW4A partners and partly funded through the programme in collaboration with the national government, Kisii county government, CSOs, and various other stakeholders. It had been hoped to officially launch the policy during that year’s 16 Days of Activism, in part due to a commitment by the county governor (see section 5.1.1), but the process took longer. Nevertheless, by Q3 of 2024 it had been approved by the county executive committee and placed before the County Assembly that approved it in early 2025, so it is now in force.
Development and adoption of Kisii County Policy on Sexual and Gender Based Violence

As a result of stakeholder engagment with key county government officials from Kisii county and cross-learning from the project counties, the Kisii County Government committed to the development of a Gender Policy that incorporates SGBV due to the deeply-entrenched patriarchal attitudes and cultural norms and practices that support the subordination of women. The WROs from Kisii, CECOME and YWCA Kenya, are part of the group drafting the Gender Policy.
no changes
Draft Kisii Gender Policy passed by the County Executive and pending approval of the County Assembly.

description.narrative: WRGE 2.1 (WRG016) # of laws to promote women’s voice, agency, leadership, and representative participation in decision-making processes in public, private and civic sphere are better implemented as a result of CSO engagement. Advocacy towards better implementation of the two-thirds gender rule

comment.narrative: The Constitution of Kenya has a two-thirds gender representation quota but there is still no legal mechanism to guarantee women’s representation in Parliament as envisaged in the Constitution and by the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court in Advisory Opinion No. 2 of 2012 held that the two-thirds gender rule required progressive implementation and further advised parliament to enact the required law on or before August 27, 2015. Draft bills have failed to garner majority support in the National Assembly therefore we will take part in any such processes to ensure the adoption of enabling legislation. In the meantime, we will advocate for the implementation of the quota at the county and national levels and encourage young women to run for elective positions.
1) Better implementation of the Migori and Meru County Policy on Sexual and Gender Based Violence 2) Better implementation of the two-thirds gender rule

Migori County: A review of the policy was conducted in June 2024 and was due to be finalised by an expert for public presentation by the Gender Department. In parallel, there is work on an SGBV bill and the governor and the county gender sector working group (GSWG) expressed their support for that early in 2024 however, as of April 2025, the draft bill was still pending discussion in the County Assembly. There seems to have been some increase in awareness of the policy among official stakeholders and community members but it is not clear whether there have been concrete improvements in implementation. During the Africa evaluation workshop in November 2024, participants from Migori suggested that better implementation is most likely if there are resources for continual follow-up.Meru CountyActions taken through the programme - development of an SGBV data collection tool in 2022, development of a community scorecard in 2023, training of Court Users Committees (CUCs) on filling some specific forms - “P3” and “PRC” - in 2024 - contributed to data collection in the courts, which in turn contributed to SGBV cases being reported separately by government and courts, to the launch of an SGBV registry, and correct filling of P3 and PRC forms. In addition, through work with the CUC and targeted lobbying, participants successfully campaigned for the establishment of a specialised SGBV Court, following the example of the establishment by the Chief Justice of such a court in Shanzu.Advocacy training of young women and media advocacy have increased awareness of community and policy makers but a call for action launched in July 2024 has still not been responded to by legislators. The county leadership have argued, incorrectly, that the Policy is just an aspirational document that does not place binding responsibility and funds cannot be allocated for its implementation. These attitudes and political instability made further progress on better implementation seem unlikely in late 2024. Nevertheless, participants from Meru in the November 2024 workshop considered that progress could still be made on strengthening the work of CUCs in this area and that they can work effectively with the finance committee, with media and in community engagements.Given the attitude of county officials to the policy, YW4A WROs, i.e YWCA Meru and Inua Mama Mjane, and the young women have also been championing an SGBV Bill that would be enforceable. They took part in its development from 2021, with support from the GSWG. Challenges with the former governor and the county government led to advocacy for it being shelved but, following a change of governor, the WROs and YW held a meeting with the new Governor in 2025 and the bill has been placed before the County Assembly for debate. The bill has the support of the governor and the GSWG, and six members of the county assembly (MCAs) are reported to be lending their support to promote its passage and implementation. A 5-person taskforce was set up to finalize the draft version of the Bill including a representative of Inua Mama Mjane. Lobbying for funding , including a courtesy call held with the Office of the Governor, the County Commissioner, WROs and young women, saw the Governor’s office and CEC for Gender commit to fast-track the adoption of the bill and to have a gender-responsive budget that supports the prevention and response to SGBV.Gender ruleIn 2023, a multi-sectoral working group delivered proposals to the Cabinet Secretary for Gender on how the rule can be implemented, including legal and statutory reforms; those proposals included some recommendations submitted by YW4A participants (see sections 4.1.2 and 5.1.1). A proposed legislative framework was developed and submitted to the Minister for Gender and Parliament in 2024. It is not clear whether the government will assign enough priority to this for it to be passed into law and, as of July 2025, parliament was yet to act on the working group's report.
4b) Better implementation of the two-thirds gender rule

The Minster for Gender set up a Multi-Sectoral Taskforce on the Implementation of the Not More than Two Third Gender Principle, which accepted submissions and technical input from the YW4A partners and young women on how to implement it. A report containing a legislative proposal (Bill) was submitted to the Minister in and is set to be tabled in Parliament
Advocacy towards better implementation of the Meru and Migori County Policies on Sexual and Gender Based Violence

The general elections held in 2022 in Kenya saw an increased number of women run for office, including a young woman under the project. Although there was a slight increase in female representation, the two-third gender rule is yet to be achieved from the highest levels of political office to the lowest, at the community and grassroot level.
